title: The nullable-scalars-and-logical-types control, measured through reconstruct() as well
rationale: Byte-identical avsc and input to avro-nullable-scalars-and-logical-types-control, which is published LOSSLESS; the only variable is the entry point. It did not start that way: this row shipped with a three-field LT schema covering two of the control's six logical types and wrapping none of them in a nullable union, while the control's requalification claimed its reconstruct() half was MEASURED. It was inferred from a neighbour that did not share the distinguishing shape. All six logical types and the nullable-union wrapping are now measured through reconstruct() on the control's own datum.
catchesBugClass: A logical-type conversion that survives reconstructToMap and breaks under the writer. Because the encode is attempted rather than merely validated, it catches a representation the schema accepts by type but the encoder rejects by size or branch - and it now covers timestamp-micros, time-millis, time-micros and uuid, which the previous three-field version did not reach at all.
cannotCatch: It says nothing about decimal, nor about a logical type nested inside an array - avro-logical-types-erased-inside-arrays owns that case and does not reach reconstruct() either. Every value is already in the wire encoding, so the string-parsing fallbacks are untouched. It also cannot separate 'union-wrapped logical types work' from 'bare logical types work'; avro-bare-logical-types-are-a-writable-datum carries the bare shape.

predicted.detail: No nested record, so the one-level copy is sufficient and the datum should validate and encode. If a union-wrapped logical type broke the writer, this is the row that would say so.
